newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia wants more carrot, less stick from EU.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia wants more carrot, less stick from EU.

text.p: New Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic criticised the European Union for its carrot-and-stick policy towards Belgrade and called for more carrot from the EU to help the country go on with reforms.
Djunic said on Monday Yugoslavia missed another chance to have its trade preferences with the European Union renewed late in March.

"I personally think the international community applies a carrot-and stick policy towards Yugoslavia by not activating previously granted trade preferentials," Djunic, in charge of reforms, economic development and relations with world financial institutions, told a news conference.
"I can understand such a strategy to some extent, but why don't they vary the order a bit. We understand a stick but let there be some carrot first," he added.
Djunic insisted lack of international help will jeopardize Yugoslavia's reforms.
"We want the world to believe we are serious about reforms, privatisation, bank rehabilitation and that we need help, both technical and financial," he added.
The Deputy Prime Minister said Yugoslavia wanted to harmonise its economy with developed countries and have an equal treatment when entering EU markets.

"If our goods are not liberated from customs duties in advance we are at a big disadvantage. In that case we cannot pursue reforms and this I call a Catch 22 situation. We need help through normal contacts with the world," he said.

Djunic insisted the government will pursue comprehensive reforms for which it needed technical help from EU's Phare programme and Know-how funds and from the U.S. USAID programme. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
